To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
KES imaging of iodinated and xenon contrast-enhanced lungs in a rat model of lung injury is feasible, and that iodine KES is superior to xenon KES in terms of image quality.
K-edge subtraction imaging using iodine contrast agents and xenon gas can be used for respiratory-gated KES lung imaging in a rat model of lung injury.

1) K-edge subtraction imaging can be used to perform respiratory-gated imaging using iodine contrast agents in a rat model, 2) K-edge imaging can be used in a rat model for respiratory-gated imaging of xenon contrast agents and 3) KES imaging can provide high quality, respiratory-gated lung images of a rat model with acute lung injury

the development of a novel imaging technique for lung imaging using iodinated contrast agent and xenon gas.
the development of a KES imaging approach for the study of lung function in a rat model of ALI.
the development of novel contrast agents and their applications in medical imaging, particularly for the diagnosis and treatment of lung diseases.

the K-edge subtraction imaging of iodine and xenion contrast agents in a rat model of ALI is feasible and provides high quality images.
